Multiple reviews showed the automation system added to the vehicle operated without issue. However, the vehicle was not able to retain a charge, which was determined to be because of a defect in the electric battery system installed by the vehicle manufacturer, Phoenix Motorcars. Over the past 5 years, METRO has been a leader in the early deployment of AV technology as an integral part of the larger public transit system. METRO’s University District Phase 1 AV Circulator project deployed an EasyMile AV shuttle as a pilot demonstration. The project tested a six-seated passenger shuttle vehicle along the half-mile-long pedestrian esplanade of the Texas Southern University (TSU) campus, known as the Tiger Walk (with an operator for safety). Source: Houston METRO The current Phase 2 deployment was first introduced to the city of Houston in December 2023 as METRO’s FutureLink Phase 2 project. The new AV shuttlebus would have been a 12-passenger seated vehicle with wheelchair provisions and ADA-compliant lifts. The vehicle would have operated in an autonomous driving mode but with a safety operator on board to test this advanced technology capability. The new vehicle would have operated within mixed traffic along city streets, having a significantly higher maximum operating speed than the Phase 1 vehicle. METRO’s “Shuttle of the Future” deployment originated from the multiphase program called the University District Project, an initiative focused on progressively testing and demonstrating AV technology for FMLM transportation that connects with regional transit systems.
